Try itA lookahead for every speed: scale it with the speed
The issue
  • A fixed 5 m is \(5/8 = 0.6\) s ahead at 8 m/s, but \(5/3.46 = 1.4\) s at 3.46 m/s.
  • Fix: scale \(L_d\) with the speed, to look the same time ahead.

  • \(L_d = \max(3\text{ m},\ k_v v)\), with \(k_v\) in seconds.
  • With \(k_v = 0.75\) s: on the approach, \(0.75 \times 8 = 6\) m; in the second arc, \(0.75 \times 3.46 = 2.6\) m, raised to 3 m.
  • Click a row to replay that run on the next part, or pick any of the 11 runs there.

Scale the lookahead with the speed
  • One rule for the whole path: the profile slows the AV in the curve, so \(L_d\) shortens there (3 m) and tracks tightly; on the straight it is 6 m and steers smoothly.
  • Our node uses \(\max(5\text{ m},\ 1\text{ s} \times v)\), since the EKF's pose jumps at each GNSS fix.
